Vignette 3, PEDIATRIC
“The Quiet Child”

Scenario Background
You are operating in a temporary field clinic following regional flooding.
Water contamination has caused a surge in diarrheal illness.
Evacuation routes are partially washed out. Nearest pediatric-capable hospital is 8–10 hours away by ground transport. Air evacuation unavailable due to weather.
It is 1900 hours. Staffing is minimal overnight.
You are the senior medical provider on site.
Location:
Basic local clinic in Zambia
Humanitarian response environment
Resource-limited infrastructure
Evacuation chain:
Next highest level of care: ~12 hours by vehicle
Nearest airstrip: ~3.5 hours by ground
Scheduled supply/mail flight (CASA C-212): 48 hours from scenario start
No immediate air evacuation available
Communications:
Spotty WiFi (video / email / VoIP intermittently functional)
Satellite phone
Radio capability
Teleconsult possible but bandwidth inconsistent
Resources:
Basic labs only
No advanced imaging
Limited resupply
Limited blood products or none depending on scenario payload

Patient
4-year-old male
 Brought in by mother
 3 days of diarrhea
 1 day of vomiting
 Decreased oral intake
 Now lethargic

Initial Assessment
Weight: 14 kg (estimate if needed)
Vitals:
HR: 148

BP: 82/50

RR: 32

SpO₂: 99% RA

Temp: 38.5°C

Cap refill: 4–5 seconds

Mental status: Withdraws to voice, not interacting

Skin: Dry mucous membranes

Sunken eyes

No rash

Abdomen soft

Urine: Mother reports no urination today.
Resources available:
IV fluids (limited)

Oral rehydration solution

Broad-spectrum antibiotics (limited)

Glucometer

No pediatric blood pressure cuffs except small adult

No lab capability

Oxygen

Basic monitor

Evacuation possible in 8–10 hours if stabilized.
